conditions: Use the original algorithm’s uniform certificate inequality together with the convex–concave saddle-point ergodic inequality, then take the supremum over comparison points to control the global gap. A small weak VI gap at a point alone does not imply a small saddle gap there.

bounds.hidden_constants: Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
bounds.witness_type_note: The variance-reduced extragradient/Mirror-Prox algorithm of Alacaoglu–Malitsky genuinely samples components and refreshes reference points randomly.

evidence.statement_summary: Expected total component calls O(n+sqrt(n)L D_K^2/epsilon) for expected Minty weak gap.
evidence.applicability_review: Source writes sum F, ours average: source components F_i/n, uniform estimator returns our F_i. Same index evaluated at two points, two charged calls. No individual component monotonicity. Full pass n. Native loopless count is expected work. Saddle-gap transfer uses source Eq12–14 and convex-concave inequality, not equivalence of output Minty gap and full saddle gap.
